proposals.before: Emperor Shenwu, posthumous temple name Gaozu of Northern Qi, bore the surname Gao; his personal name was Huan and his style Heiliuhun. He came from Tiao in Bohai.
proposals.after: Gaozu Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi bore the surname Gao; his personal name was Huan and his style Heiliuhun. He came from Tiao in Bohai.
proposals.reason: 高祖 is the temple name (廟號) and 神武 the posthumous name (諡號); 'posthumous temple name Gaozu' conflates the two.

proposals.before: After Gao Huan rose to power he posthumously enfeoffed Duan Chang as Minister of Works and brought his son Ning into office.
proposals.after: After Gao Huan rose to power he posthumously honored Duan Chang with the title Minister of Works and brought his son Ning into office.
proposals.reason: 追贈司空 is a posthumous grant of the office/title Minister of Works, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: When Gao Huan was born his mother Lady Han died, and he was reared in the household of his full elder sister's husband Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.
proposals.after: When Gao Huan was born his mother Lady Han died, and he was reared in the household of his full elder sister's husband Wei Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉景 is the full name Wei/Yu Jing; English drops the surname 尉 and leaves only Jing.

proposals.before: Liu Gui once came by a white hawk and went hunting on the open steppe with Gao Huan, Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, Jia Xianzhi, and the rest.
proposals.after: Liu Gui once came by a white hawk and went hunting on the open steppe with Gao Huan, Wei Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, Jia Xianzhi, and the rest.
proposals.reason: Jing here continues 尉景; the surname should be retained for clarity with Hou Jing also in the chapter.

proposals.before: Disgusted by Luozhou's methods, he secretly plotted with Jing, Duan Rong, and Cai Jun.
proposals.after: Disgusted by Luozhou's methods, he secretly plotted with Wei Jing, Duan Rong, and Cai Jun.
proposals.reason: Chinese gives the full name 尉景; English "Jing" alone drops the surname 尉 and obscures the referent.

proposals.before: Wenxiang and the Empress Dowager of Yongxi of Wei were both young; Empress Wuming on the ox bore them in her arms.
proposals.after: Wenxiang and the Empress Yongxi of Wei were both young; Empress Wuming on the ox bore them in her arms.
proposals.reason: 魏永熙后 is the empress associated with the Yongxi emperor, not an empress dowager; "Empress Dowager" mistranslates 后.

proposals.before: Wenxiang kept falling from the ox; Gao Huan strung his bow as if to shoot the boy dead and be rid of the burden.
proposals.after: Wenxiang kept falling from the ox; Gao Huan bent his bow intending to shoot him to decide whether to abandon the flight.
proposals.reason: 決去 means deciding whether to leave/give up the undertaking, not merely discarding a burden by killing the child.

proposals.before: Zhao refused heed, killed the emperor, and with Erzhu Shilong and others enthroned Prince Changguang of Changguang, changing the era name to Jianming.
proposals.after: Zhao refused to heed him, killed the emperor, and with Erzhu Shilong and others enthroned Ye, Prince of Changguang, changing the era name to Jianming.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長廣王曄 is Ye, Prince of Changguang; 'Prince Changguang of Changguang' doubles the fief name and drops the personal name 曄.

proposals.before: Gao Huan struck him with his fist and broke a tooth, saying, "In the days of the Heavenly Pillar you crawled to his commands like hunting dogs. The realm now rests with you, my lord, yet this flatterer dares deceive you—I ask leave to kill him."
proposals.after: Gao Huan struck him with his fist and broke a tooth, saying, "In the days of the Heavenly Pillar you fellows submitted to orders like hawks and hounds. The realm now rests with you, my lord, yet Ajuni dares deceive those below and mislead those above—I ask leave to kill him."
proposals.reason: Chinese names 阿鞠泥 (Ajuni); idiomatic replaces him with 'this flatterer' and softens 奴輩 / 誣下罔上.

proposals.before: Jing had hidden strong men ready to seize Zhao; Gao Huan bit his arm to stop him, saying, "Kill him now and his faction will scatter and regroup.
proposals.after: Wei Jing had hidden strong men ready to seize Zhao; Gao Huan bit his arm to stop him, saying, "Kill him now and his faction will scatter and regroup.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉景 should keep the surname; bare 'Jing' obscures the referent.

proposals.before: Later the Shangdang exiles at Jinyang lived in what was called Shangdang Ward—and Gao Huan had lived there.
proposals.after: Later those from Shangdang living at Jinyang formed what was called Shangdang Ward—and Gao Huan had lived there.
proposals.reason: Chinese 上黨人居晉陽者 means people from Shangdang residing at Jinyang, not specifically exiles.

proposals.before: Near and far men praised Commandant Gao for his disciplined troops and gave him their hearts.
proposals.after: Near and far men praised Gao, Equal in Ceremonies, for his disciplined troops and gave him their hearts.
proposals.reason: 儀同 is the honorific title Equal in Ceremonies (儀同三司), not the office Commandant.

proposals.before: He called up ten thousand men to send away; Sun Teng and Jing twice asked for a five-day delay.
proposals.after: He called up ten thousand men to send away; Sun Teng and Wei Jing twice asked for a five-day delay.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉景 is the full name Wei Jing; English reduces him to the ambiguous bare given name Jing.

proposals.before: He mobilized ten thousand men and was about to send them off; Sun Teng and Jing asked that they be kept five days — twice thus.
proposals.after: He mobilized ten thousand men and was about to send them off; Sun Teng and Wei Jing asked that they be kept five days — twice thus.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉景 should be rendered Wei Jing in full, matching the personal name in the source.

proposals.before: March west and you die; miss the deadline and you die; be handed to the Jie-Hu and you die—what can we do?"
proposals.after: March west and you die; miss the deadline and you die; be assigned among the ruling peoples and you die—what can we do?"
proposals.reason: Chinese 配國人 means assignment to the regime's own people (國人), not the Jie-Hu (契胡) of the prior forged letter.

proposals.before: On the renyin day of the tenth month they upheld Prince Lang, son of Prince Zhangwu Rong and Bohai governor, as emperor, era name Zhongxing — this was the Deposed Emperor.
proposals.after: On the renyin day of the tenth month they upheld Lang, son of Prince Zhangwu Rong and Bohai governor, as emperor, era name Zhongxing — this was the Deposed Emperor.
proposals.reason: Chinese 朗 is the personal name being enthroned; rendering him already as 'Prince Lang' invents a princely title the sentence does not give him.

proposals.before: In the intercalary third month Erzhu Tianguang marched from Chang'an, Zhao from Bing Province, Dulü from Luoyang, and Zhongyuan from Dong Commandery to meet at Ye with a force said to number two hundred thousand. They camped along the Huan River while Emperor Jiemin put Changsun Chengye in overall command as Grand Eastern Chief.
proposals.after: In the intercalary third month Erzhu Tianguang marched from Chang'an, Zhao from Bing Province, Dulü from Luoyang, and Zhongyuan from Dong Commandery to meet at Ye with a force said to number two hundred thousand. They camped along the Huan River while Emperor Jiemin put Changsun Chengye in overall command as Grand Chief of the Eastern Headquarters.
proposals.reason: 大行臺總督 is the Grand Chief/Director of the Branch Department (行臺), not a vague 'Grand Eastern Chief'.

proposals.before: Before the battle, in the month prior, Zhang Shao of Zhangwu was seized at night by several horsemen who carried him over the wall to a great general. He was ordered to guide the army toward Ye for one who had received Heaven's mandate to destroy the wicked.
proposals.after: Before the battle, in the month prior, Zhang Shao of Zhangwu was seized at night by several horsemen who carried him over the wall to a great general. He was ordered to guide the army toward Ye, it being said they would assist the one who had received Heaven's mandate in destroying the wicked.
proposals.reason: Chinese 佐受命者除殘賊 means assisting the mandate-holder to eliminate the wicked; the idiomatic line drops 佐 and collapses the syntax.

proposals.before: At Xiurong Zhao split his forces to hold the passes and raided back and forth.
proposals.after: Once Erzhu Zhao had reached Xiurong, he split his forces to hold the passes and raided back and forth.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic fuses place-name Xiurong with personal name Zhao, obscuring that Erzhu Zhao is the subject who had arrived at Xiurong.

proposals.before: Husi Chun was inwardly ill at ease; with Prince Nanyang Baoqu and Military Guard Generals Yuan Pi, Wei Guang, and Wang Sizheng he slandered Gao Huan to the Wei emperor.
proposals.after: Husi Chun was inwardly ill at ease; with Prince Nanyang Baoju and Military Guard Generals Yuan Pi, Wei Guang, and Wang Sizheng he slandered Gao Huan to the Wei emperor.
proposals.reason: Chinese 寶炬 transliterates as Baoju; Baoqu is a clear mistransliteration of the personal name.

proposals.before: Husi Chun was inwardly ill at ease from this; with Prince Nanyang Baoqu and Military Guard Generals Yuan Pi, Wei Guang, and Wang Sizheng he slandered Shenwu to the Wei emperor.
proposals.after: Husi Chun was inwardly ill at ease from this; with Prince Nanyang Baoju and Military Guard Generals Yuan Pi, Wei Guang, and Wang Sizheng he slandered Shenwu to the Wei emperor.
proposals.reason: Chinese 寶炬 transliterates as Baoju; Baoqu is a clear mistransliteration of the personal name.

decisions.reason: 齊高祖神武皇帝 places temple name 高祖 before posthumous name 神武; 'posthumous temple name Gaozu' wrongly merges 廟號 and 諡號, and the proposed order matches the Chinese.
追贈長司空 is a posthumous grant of the Minister of Works title, not an enfeoffment; 'honored ... with the title' is accurate.
Chinese 尉景 is the full name; bare 'Jing' drops the surname 尉 and leaves the husband unidentified.
The hunting party lists 尉景 in full; English 'Jing' omits the surname and risks confusion with Hou Jing later in the chapter.
私與尉景、段榮、蔡儁圖之 gives the full name 尉景; restoring Wei Jing removes the bare-given-name ambiguity.
魏永熙后 is the empress of the Yongxi reign, not an empress dowager; 后 does not mean 太后 here.
將射之以決去 means shooting to decide whether to abandon the flight; 'be rid of the burden' misses 決去.
立長廣王曄 names Ye, Prince of Changguang; 'Prince Changguang of Changguang' doubles the fief and drops 曄.
The speech names 阿鞠泥 and has 奴輩…如鷹犬 and 誣下罔上; replacing Ajuni with 'this flatterer' and softening those phrases is inaccurate.
尉景伏壯士 keeps the surname; bare 'Jing' obscures who prepared to seize Zhao.
上黨人居晉陽者 are people from Shangdang living at Jinyang; 'exiles' is not in the Chinese.
高儀同 is the honorific 儀同 (Equal in Ceremonies), not the office Commandant.
孫騰、尉景 names Wei Jing in full; bare Jing is ambiguous beside other Jing figures.
The literal field likewise drops the surname from 尉景; Wei Jing restores the source name.
配國人 is assignment among the regime's own people, not the Jie-Hu named only in the prior forged letter.
奉…渤海太守朗為皇帝 gives personal name Lang and office Bohai governor; 'Prince Lang' invents a princely title.
大行臺總督 is overall command as Grand Chief of the Branch/Eastern Headquarters, not a vague Grand Eastern Chief.
云佐受命者除殘賊 includes 佐 'assist'; the mandate-holder; the old English dropped that verb.
尒朱兆旣至秀容 makes Erzhu Zhao the subject who had reached Xiurong; 'At Xiurong Zhao' fuses place and name.
南陽王寶炬 transliterates as Baoju; Baoqu is a mistransliteration of 炬.
The literal field repeats Baoqu for 寶炬; Baoju is the correct transliteration.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0020 restores Baoju for 寶炬; the English personal-name value Baoqu came only from the bad transliteration.
Accepted r0020 restores Baoju in the title claim; Prince Nanyang Baoqu was created by the same mistransliteration of 寶炬.
